touches.text: Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Inference Ticket: the record of one call to the inference proxy, everything that happened to that request.
Transient: the transient tree (what the logging tree becomes).
Owns the transient tree and its 30 day sweep (4.3.2.3).
INTENTION:
To the Tester (11, CodeMother's machine): test, proofgate (hook: proofs run by hand)
To CC (12): mailcheck, askscan, turnscan, artifactgate, deletegate (all Claude Code hooks), slate, skilldial
CODEMOTHER DEVICE (cairn/devices/codemother/)

Owns the inspectors and gates (draft, moving from standalone): build_inspector, plan_inspector, ticket_inspector, corrosion, exemptions, rehearsal, determinism, import_sieve, and the tester (11; Q#33, Akien 2026-10-29). (Not diagnostic_inspector: it is base's, 17.3.) The code pipeline's inspectors and gates move to CodeMother; any that are not about code (if such existed) would not. (Q#31, Akien 2026-10-27)
TESTER MACHINE, CodeMother's (was the tester device, cairn/devices/tester/)
INTENTION:
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
TOOLS: base, validation_store, proof_coverage, scratch, question, proof_discovery, chain, bus_client, artifact, system_word; machines ruling, build_inspector; db client
VERBS: run, notices — CodeMother's verbs, reached over the bus (RULE 1)
COMMANDS: cairn test (--hollow, --seal, --exec, …) → cairn codemother test, the CLI a client of her verb
CC DEVICE (cairn/devices/cc/)
Owns the Claude Code hooks (5.10.5): mail check, the turn-shape and ask scans, the gates on record writes and deletes.
Every call makes an inference ticket (3.3.2): trees first, then the cheapest route the nest finds.
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.

ROOT INTENTION for checks and gates (Akien, 2026-10-27): the inspector does all the checks, so there is no need for more checks anywhere else. The inspector's output is consumed by the gate. The gate's output is the certificate. "This was how I meant it all along."

open_questions.text: `commit` and `cross` are verbs here: is moving a ticket across its workflow CodeMother's job (she owns the workflows), or the ticket's (it owns its refusals, 3.3.1.5)?
Claude Code itself calls Anthropic directly, around the proxy. Is that "an error" to fix someday (CC's calls routed through it), or is CC outside the rule as an external device?
